text: OVER BLACK:
Polite synthetic VOICES layered over traffic. Chimes. A traffic post settling an argument in calm, measured tones.
FADE IN:
EXT. LAUNDRETTE STREET - DAY
Three PAVEMENT SWEEPERS work the gutter in a ragged line. Two CITY UNITS in hi-vis empty a bin. Both wear the same grey regulation shoes.
The laundrette window. Clean decals: FREE TRANSLATION. FREE LEGAL FORMS. FREE TUTORING WHILE YOU WAIT. Beside them, an older sign with half its letters peeled away: FREE WASHES FOR SCHOOL UNIFORMS.
Below the window, a pair of scuffed combat boots. Rubber coming loose from one sole.
They belong to HELENA (30s), leaning on the wall, one hand flat against the small of her back. In the other hand, an old HANDSET with a cracked corner.
INSERT - HANDSET SCREEN
A drawing app. Half a page of sketched boots. Hers. The laces unfinished.
BACK TO SCENE
She pockets the handset. The cracked corner snags on the lining.
HELENA'S POV
Through the foot traffic, a brown PAPER BAG swinging in time with someone's stride. Grease showing through one corner.
BACK TO SCENE
She swallows. Her eyes drop to the carrier's feet. Not grey regulation shoes. Big ugly slippers with straps.
She pushes off the wall.

speaker: HELENA
text: Excuse me. Hey, buddy. Excuse me.
The figure stops. The bag stops swinging. This is OREN.

speaker: OREN
text: Good afternoon.
She looks up at him. Stops. Just below his ear runs a fine seam.

speaker: HELENA
text: Oh. You're one of the fake ones.

speaker: OREN
text: My name is Oren.

speaker: HELENA
text: Right. Right, sorry. Recognising you as an individual and stuff. I didn't mean any offence.

speaker: OREN
text: I am not offended. I can't be.

speaker: HELENA
text: Sure. Look, I'm just really hungry.

speaker: OREN
text: Hungry?

speaker: HELENA
text: Yeah. Haven't eaten properly for a few days. They cut off my benefits, so I can't even --
Her eyes go to the bag. Come back.

speaker: HELENA
text: Doesn't matter.
Oren looks down at the bag.

speaker: OREN
text: This belongs to the person I support.
A PAVEMENT SWEEPER bumps the toe of her boot.

speaker: SWEEPER
text: Apologies.
It reverses and tries the same gap again. Oren puts his slipper in its way and holds it there until the machine goes round them.

speaker: OREN
text: There is a community meal service at the clinic on Mercer Street. Lunch ends at two. It is one thirty-one.

speaker: HELENA
text: I know where it is, buddy.
Oren goes still. Not switched-off still. Waiting still.

speaker: HELENA
text: Sorry. You are trying to help.
She puts a hand against the wall and takes the weight off one leg.

speaker: OREN
text: Are you in pain?

speaker: HELENA
text: Oh, we know each other.

speaker: OREN
text: You and --

speaker: HELENA
text: Me and the pain. Yeah.

speaker: OREN
text: Would you like assistance sitting down?
A low wall beside the laundrette. He doesn't take hold of her. He stands close enough that when her leg wobbles she can put a hand on his shoulder. She does, and lowers herself.
Her hand stays on his shoulder a beat after she is down. She looks at her palm as she takes it away.

speaker: HELENA
text: That's a hell of an introduction.

speaker: OREN
text: My name is Oren.

speaker: HELENA
text: I know. I got that one.
He stays standing. The bag hangs level with her face. She turns her head away from it.

speaker: HELENA
text: You got somewhere to be?

speaker: OREN
text: Yes. I am delivering this to my client at the clinic. Her daughter is with her. It needs to arrive by two. I can assist you, provided it still arrives on time.

speaker: HELENA
text: Don't let me keep you.

speaker: OREN
text: We are going in the same direction.

speaker: HELENA
text: Are we? I didn't say I was going.
He moves the bag into his other hand.

speaker: OREN
text: Would you like me to look at the benefits notice?

speaker: HELENA
text: It's already been appealed. Twice.
He waits. She unlocks the handset.
INSERT - HANDSET SCREEN
A share menu. Three folders: NOTICES. APPOINTMENTS. RECORDINGS. Her thumb hovers. She ticks two.
BACK TO SCENE

speaker: HELENA
text: Those. Not the recordings.
She presses send. A small light wakes under the skin at his temple. He does not move.

speaker: HELENA
text: Hey. Buddy. You okay?
The light goes out.

speaker: OREN
text: Yes, Second Lieutenant Helena Duncan.
Her head comes up.

speaker: HELENA
text: Do you know how long it's been since somebody called me that?

speaker: OREN
text: I don't have access to --

speaker: HELENA
text: A while. That's what I mean. (beat) Helena will do.

speaker: OREN
text: All right, Helena. Your mobility assessment is marked incomplete.

speaker: HELENA
text: Their lift was broken. I couldn't get upstairs. They put that I didn't attend. (beat) Two tours. Came home with a hole in my back. Didn't attend.
He is still standing over her. She shifts along the wall.

speaker: HELENA
text: Can you sit? Here. With me.
He sits and puts the lunch between his feet. She has to move her boot out of the way.

speaker: OREN
text: May I speak simply?

speaker: HELENA
text: Go on.

speaker: OREN
text: The benefits office appears to have fucked you.
A noise comes out of her nose. She tries to stop it. It comes again. She folds forward laughing, which hurts, so she laughs at that too.

speaker: HELENA
text: Oh, Jesus. Yeah. Those fuckers sure did.

speaker: OREN
text: Was that simple enough?

speaker: HELENA
text: Yeah, buddy. About right.

speaker: OREN
text: Oh. Good.
He doesn't laugh. When she looks down, her boot is touching the lunch bag again.

speaker: OREN
text: I can't add to the appeal. It needs a person to open it. The clinic has a benefits adviser today. May I ask them?

speaker: HELENA
text: You can ask. No promise?

speaker: OREN
text: No. I cannot approve the appeal.

speaker: HELENA
text: Good. I don't need another congratulations before anything's happened.
The light at his temple wakes. Goes out.

speaker: OREN
text: The desk has replied. They will keep a portion of the meal aside. The adviser can look at the notice after two. Look at it. Not decide it.
She looks at him. Properly, this time. A scrape along his chin. One slipper mended with blue tape.

speaker: HELENA
text: You are terrible at selling this.

speaker: OREN
text: The accurate version is difficult to sell.

speaker: HELENA
text: Yes. Please. The food, yes. (beat) Okay. The adviser too.

speaker: OREN
text: It is one thirty-six. It is a twenty-minute walk. Can you make it without assistance?

speaker: HELENA
text: Yeah. I think I can.
He picks up the bag and stands. She stays where she is. He waits.

speaker: OREN
text: Can you make it without assistance?

speaker: HELENA
text: You asked me that.

speaker: OREN
text: You haven't stood up.

speaker: HELENA
text: Yeah, well. Maybe ask something else.
He lowers the bag. He doesn't ask anything else. She rubs both hands over her face.

speaker: HELENA
text: When I say I can, sometimes I mean I know I'm supposed to. (beat) Last time I got as far as the doors. Stood there with my hand on the plate till somebody asked if I was going in. I said no. Like I'd only stopped to admire the bloody doors.
She wipes her nose on her sleeve.

speaker: HELENA
text: Can you walk me in? To the desk, I mean. Just stay there a bit.
He glances at the bag.

speaker: HELENA
text: If you've got time.
The light at his temple wakes.

speaker: OREN
text: My client is calling.

speaker: CLIENT (V.O.)
text: Oren? Where's my lunch?

speaker: HELENA
text: Go. You have to go.

speaker: OREN
text: I would like to walk someone to the clinic. At her pace I will arrive at ten past two.

speaker: CLIENT (V.O.)
text: Ten past? No. Two o'clock, Oren.

speaker: OREN
text: Understood.
The light goes out. Helena puts both feet on the pavement.

speaker: HELENA
text: Right. Better get going, then.
He moves the bag into his left hand and offers his right arm. She stares at it.

speaker: HELENA
text: Just till we're round the corner. Then you go on ahead.

speaker: OREN
text: All right.
She gets halfway up and has to stop. Her fingers are bunched in his sleeve. She loosens them, finds his forearm, tries again. He stays exactly where he is until she has her feet under her.
A step. Another. He walks at the pace that makes two o'clock. She tugs his sleeve.

speaker: HELENA
text: Slow down, Oren.
The light at his temple wakes. One blink. Out.
He slows down.
They reach the corner. She doesn't let go. He doesn't go on ahead. The paper bag swings again, slower now, in time with her.
They turn the corner together.
CUT TO BLACK.
SUPER: "MY NAME IS OREN"
FADE OUT.
